name: Environmental movement
title: The story of the environmental movement

text: About 200 years ago, the poet William Wordsworth called the Lake District “a sort of national property” for all who loved it.
In America, Henry David Thoreau wrote that people should live close to nature.
src: Early in the 19th century the poet William Wordsworth called the Lake District “a sort of national property in which every man has a right and interest who has an eye to perceive and a heart to enjoy”
Henry David Thoreau’s Walden (1854) argued that people should become intimately close with nature

text: Factories burned more and more coal, and their smoke filled the air of the towns.
People began campaigns against the smoke and to save the countryside, forests and wild animals.
src: The great factories of the Industrial Revolution and the immense growth in coal burning brought unprecedented air pollution to industrial centres
the movement grew from campaigns against the smoke of the Industrial Revolution and from the defence of countryside, forests and wildlife in the 19th century

text: In Britain, an artist tired of the coal smoke started a society to fight it.
After a deadly smog in London more than 70 years ago, Britain passed a law for cleaner air.
src: The artist Sir William Blake Richmond, frustrated by the pall of coal smoke, founded the Coal Smoke Abatement Society
London’s Great Smog of 1952, which may have caused upward of 6,000 deaths, led to the Clean Air Act 1956

text: More than 60 years ago, a book by Rachel Carson called Silent Spring helped start the movement of today.
In Brazil, indigenous communities and rubber tappers protected much of the rainforest with blockades.
src: 1962: Rachel Carson publishes Silent Spring / The roots of the contemporary movement are traced to Rachel Carson’s Silent Spring
in Brazil indigenous communities and rubber tappers carried out blockades that protected much rainforest

text: Since then it has campaigned against acid rain, damage to the ozone layer and the cutting down of forests.
Today it is a worldwide movement of many groups that do not always agree, and climate change worries it most.
src: acid rain in the 1980s, ozone depletion and deforestation in the 1990s
It is an international movement of many organisations and approaches, not always united in its goals / today is much concerned with climate change
